limits_basis: The heaviest allowed run of each scenario takes at most about 12 s in headless Chromium on the build machine (a fast 2025 laptop CPU), which leaves a factor of two and more for a slower laptop: under about 30 s. Heaviest means the smallest signature (S22-minB-5K, most transactions per block) at the highest allowed gas limit, 4 measured slots, the scenario's own mode. A run over time_limit_s is stopped by the engine. The campaign's tables are 40-node runs; only F3 reaches that size inside the limits.

ids.name: 8141 full
ids.description: The signature rides in a frame transaction as opaque bytes and the account's own EVM code verifies it; signatures verified that way cannot be aggregated later.

ids.name: 8141 light
ids.description: leanSPHINCS joins EIP-8141's built-in signature list next to secp256k1 and P256, clients verify it natively, and the same accounts can be aggregated later.

ids.name: 8288 light, raw signatures
ids.description: The transaction declares its signature as an EIP-8288 dependency but there is no proof yet: raw signatures go in the block and every node checks them.

ids.name: 8288 light, builder proves
ids.description: Raw signatures gossip in the mempool with no recursion, and only the builder proves them, with one STARK per block.

limits.reason: the configuration fixes 40 nodes (one uplink per node, degree 32) and one run takes about a minute in the browser (36 s natively); with override_limits, measured_slots 1 and mode run it takes about 16 s

ids.name: 8288 or leanPCS, gas binds
ids.description: Mempool nodes aggregate recursively every second and the block carries one STARK. The signature is an EIP-8288 dependency in both designs; throughput is capped by the flat gas charged for it, 33,000 in EIP-8288 and 3,000 in the leanPCS draft.

limits.reason: above 60 M gas the prover binds and the capacity search needs 6 to 8 runs: 26 s at 12 nodes and 200 M, a minute at 24 nodes and 300 M

ids.name: 8288 or leanPCS, mempool binds
ids.description: Same design, but the limit is provers or node uplinks, because peers keep exchanging proofs of about 300 KB.

ids.name: Signature inside a user-side proof
ids.description: No signature scheme is enshrined: the user's laptop, the first hop or a bundler proves the signature inside a STARK and a contract checks it through leanPCS claims. The leanPCS draft does not handle plain signatures this way.
ids.route: one signature per transaction, proved on the user's host
